chains.title: GABPA gain-of-binding at the TERT promoter

links.claim: The alt A allele is predicted to bind GABPA more strongly than ref G. This is supported by the GABPA own QBiC-SELEX model (alt effect +4.05, z 71.32; alt site 99.8th vs ref 96.3rd percentile), and by Ets-family mapped models with the same direction. GABPA ChIP peaks over this base only in HepG2/SK-N-SH, not in a glioblastoma-matching biosample, so occupancy in the disease context is not established.
The variant lies in a promoter-like cCRE, EH38E3622530, with DNase, H3K27ac, and H3K4me3 signals consistent with an active promoter element.
TERT is the nearest gene, 0 kb from its TSS, and the variant is annotated as a TERT upstream gene variant.
GABPA is expressed in DepMap glioblastoma context, and TERT is a disease-relevant gene across glioblastoma, melanoma, and bladder cancer, although the disease links are broad.
If GABPA activates TERT at this promoter, the alt allele would increase TERT expression and promote tumor phenotypes. This activator role at TERT is not directly shown by the available evidence.

predictions: Allele-specific GABPA ChIP or reporter assays would show alt > ref activity at this base in a relevant cellular context.
GABPA depletion would reduce TERT expression when the alt allele is present.
The alt allele would increase TERT promoter activity in a GABPA-dependent manner.
falsified_if: Allele-specific GABPA ChIP in a relevant heterozygous disease-model cell line shows no alt > ref occupancy over this base.
A TERT promoter reporter with the G and A alleles shows no alt-specific increase in the relevant cellular context.
GABPA perturbation does not change TERT expression in an allele-dependent manner.

chains.title: ZNF143 loss-of-repressor binding at the TERT promoter

links.claim: The ref G allele is predicted to bind ZNF143 more strongly than alt A. QBiC-SELEX supports this (effect -0.649, z -11.71; ref site 100.0th vs alt 98.4th percentile), but ZNF143 has an ENCODE peak over this base only in GM12878, not in the disease context.
The variant lies in a promoter-like active cCRE, making allele-specific repressor loss at a promoter plausible.
TERT is the nearest gene and is annotated as the affected upstream gene.
ZNF143 is expressed in DepMap glioblastoma context, and TERT is broadly relevant to the listed cancers.

If ZNF143 represses TERT at this promoter, loss of ZNF143 binding on the alt allele would derepress TERT and promote disease. The available ZNF143/TERT literature search did not directly establish this repressor role.

predictions: Allele-specific ZNF143 ChIP would show ref > alt occupancy at this base in relevant cells.
The alt allele would increase TERT reporter activity if ZNF143 is a repressor.
ZNF143 knockdown or overexpression would modulate TERT in the predicted repressive direction.
falsified_if: Allele-specific ZNF143 ChIP in a relevant background shows no ref > alt occupancy at this base.
The alt allele does not reduce ZNF143-dependent repression of a TERT reporter.
ZNF143 acts as an activator rather than a repressor of TERT in the relevant context.

chains.title: TGIF2 loss-of-repressor binding at the TERT promoter

links.claim: The ref G allele is predicted to bind TGIF2 more strongly than alt A. QBiC-SELEX supports this (effect -1.113, z -12.19; ref site 98.3rd vs alt 71.5th percentile), but TGIF2 has an ENCODE peak over this base only in HepG2, not in the disease context.
The variant is in an active promoter-like cCRE, so allele-specific loss of a repressor could affect promoter output.
TERT is the nearest gene and the variant is upstream of TERT.
TGIF2 is expressed in glioblastoma DepMap data, and TERT is broadly relevant to the listed cancers.
If TGIF2 represses TERT, the alt allele would reduce TGIF2 binding and increase TERT expression. No direct evidence shows TGIF2 represses TERT.

QBiC-SELEX screen of chr5:1295135:G>A, one line per TF, each with the TF's own or CIS-BP-mapped model of largest |z|. Candidates are TFs whose ENCODE ChIP-seq peaks contain the variant and that are expressed (DepMap subtype median Glioblastoma), bound here before bound elsewhere, then a strong site before a weak one, then by |z|; then expressed TFs ENCODE never assayed whose best model passes the gate (occupancy unknown). Shown: 10 of 18 occupied (14 with a strong site), 5 of 145 with unknown occupancy. Left out: 0 TFs assayed in the matching biosample and 554 assayed only elsewhere, none with a peak here; 1 bound but below 1 TPM. The gate (|z| > 4.05, Bonferroni over 997 models) marks a change QBiC-SELEX detects; it says nothing about occupancy. Effect > 0 means the alternate allele binds more strongly. In vitro binding only. Site strength is the better allele's best k-mer over the variant, as a percentile of the best model's k-mers; a strong site reaches the 97.5th. At a weak site the ChIP peak more likely reflects another site in the element.
